contexts.text: This is the sea of salt () = the foul things of the Falsities... For the sea of salt = the Falsities which break forth from cupidities.
As cupidities and Falsities are what vastate man... vastation is described by saltness. Illustrated.
Sulphur = the vastation of good; salt, the vastation of truth; for parching and saltness destroy the land and its products, as cupidity destroys goods, and Falsity truths.
As salt signified vastation, it was customary to sow with salt the cities they destroyed, that they might not be rebuilt (). AC 2455:end.
Salt, in the contrary sense, = that which gives fertility, and as it were savour.
The fourth state (of that Church), that the affection of truth perishes, is Lot's wife becoming a statue of salt.
She became a statue of salt () = that all the good of truth was vastated. AC 10300:7.
Salt, in the genuine sense, = the affection of truth; in the opposite, the vastation of the affection of truth, that is, of the good in truth. Illustrated.
A salt land () = truths vastated.
To be given to salt () = to be vastated.
Love, without holy fear, is like something unsalted, or like food in which there is no salt, and thence no savour; but love with fear is like food salted, which however does not taste of salt.
The extinction of interior truth is signified by Abimelech destroying that city and sowing it with salt ().
Ye are the salt of the earth () = the truth of the Church, which longs for good. Salt which has lost its savour = truth devoid of a longing for good (which is good for nothing).

To be salted with fire () = the longing of good for truth; and to be salted with salt = the longing of truth for good; salt which has lost its saltness = truth devoid of a longing for good; to have salt in themselves = this longing.

Salt is good () = truth longing for good; salt which has lost its savour = truth devoid of a longing for good (which is fit for no use whatever, good or evil). Those in such truth are those called lukewarm.

Every... meat-offering shall be salted with salt; neither shalt thou cease to make the salt of the covenant of thy God upon thy meat-offering; upon every gift thou shalt offer salt () = that the longing of truth for good, and of good for truth, was [to be] in all worship; hence, too, that salt is called the salt of the covenant of God; for covenant = conjunction; and salt = the longing for conjunction. AC 10137:end. AC 10300:4. AE 701:28.

The reason salt = the longing of truth, is that salt renders the land fertile, and makes food savoury; and because in salt there is what is fiery and at the same time conjunctive, as in truth there is an ardent longing for good, and at the same time what is conjunctive.
A statue of salt = the disjunction (of good) from truth; for salt, in the opposite sense, = the destruction and vastation of truth. Illustrated. AC 9207:6.

Salt () = the longing of truth for good. (Thus the healing of the waters by Elisha with salt) = the amendment of the Church and of the life through the Word, and through the derivative longing of truth for good. AC 10300:end.

Salted () = the longing of truth for good; (for) salt = the longing of the love of truth for good; hence what is salted = that in which there is this longing. The reason there ought to be a longing of truth for good, is that this longing is conjunctive of both... The conjunction of good and truth is what is called the heavenly marriage, which is Heaven itself with man; and therefore, when, in Divine worship, and in each and all things of it, there is a longing for this conjunction, there is Heaven in each and all things there, thus the Lord, This is signified by [the requirement] that the incense was to be salted.
The reason salt has this signification, is from its conjunctive nature; for it conjoins all things, and hence gives them savour; nay, it conjoins water and oil, which otherwise are not conjoined.

When it is known that by salt is signified the longing for the conjunction of truth and good, it may be known what is signified (in ): everyone must be salted with fire = that everyone must long from genuine love; every sacrifice must be salted with salt = that the longing from genuine love must be in all worship; salt which has lost its saltness = a longing from some other love than a genuine one; to have salt in themselves = the longing of truth for good.
So in ... salt which has lost its savour = a longing from the proprium, thus from the love of self and of the world: such a longing is salt which has lost its savour; it is not fit for anything.

As the longing of truth for good conjoins, so the longing of falsity for evil disjoins, and that which disjoins also destroys; hence salt, in the opposite sense, = the destruction and devastation of truth and good. Illustrated.
He shall dwell in parched places and in a salt land () = in filthy loves and their longings, which have destroyed the good and truth of the Church.
A pit of salt () = a longing for falsity; which, as it destroys truth and good, is called a waste to eternity ( = the devastation of all truth. AE 653:6.)
(Thus) salt, in the genuine sense, = the longing of truth for good, thus what is conjunctive; and, in the opposite, the longing of falsity for evil, thus what is destructive.
That the blood nourishes itself from the air... is evident, also, from the immense abundance of salts of various kinds [which are] in company with the water from the earth, rivers, and lakes.
Salt () = a longing for truth.
(Such) become statues of salt.

Salt is what causes savour, nay, odour; for without salt [anything] is insipid and flat; there is therefore a keenness and very force in it which excites the sense. This, therefore, is salt () namely, that it is to be done with sense, thought, and perception.
Without suitable repugnances, there is no stimulus.

On the poisonous acute sayings (of Gustaf Benzelstierna). - He could pour out such acute sayings against others, that they could not be answered; for he so turned them that he against whom he poured them, became as it were stupid, and angry that he could not retort... As he supposed himself to be more learned than others, he was inspired to pour out such acute sayings. Example(s). (His sphere described.) DMin 4760. Described.

On the almost irresistible acutenesses of man. - Anton. Swab could speak with such intelligence, modesty, and semblance of reason, as could scarcely be resisted. Such acutenesses, with the evil ... were represented by the head of a certain animal... from which went forth coarse spicula of salt, of a yellow colour. (Diagram.) It was... poison salts, which, when they puncture, cannot be plucked away, and at the same time they infuse poison.
To go away into salt () = not to receive spiritual life, but to remain in a life merely natural. (Compare AE 513:7.)
Salt () = the vastation of all truth through falsities from these concupiscences.
Saltness () = the devastation of truth through falsities.
(If the affection which is in every employment be not relaxed by diversions) it becomes dull... like salt when it has lost its saltness, whence there is no excitation, nor stimulus.
